note: The clinician's governance surface. Evaluated top to bottom: the first matching base rule sets the starting rung, then every matching modifier adjusts it. Budget and language only shift the suggestion and add tags — they never remove a rung from view. PROVISIONAL until clinician sign-off.

baseRules.because: A severe band with a long history needs the most intensive rung Reitti can point to.
A severe band, even when recent, warrants individual professional care.
Moderately-severe and long-standing points to individual therapy rather than a group.
Moderately-severe but recent is well served by structured online therapy.
A moderate band is the evidence-based home of nettiterapia and professional groups.
Mild difficulty responds well to peer support and community options.
No band raised — self-help and prevention are the right starting point.

modifiers.because: A long-standing difficulty biases one rung up, because lower rungs have usually been tried already.
A positive trauma screen adds a trauma-informed provider tag; it does not change intensity by itself.
Risky drinking adds substance-aware resources alongside the suggestion; it is not a rung on its own.
No budget for private care shifts the suggestion toward free and public options — nothing is hidden.
Loneliness or a social domain makes a group the better-value first step.
A language other than Finnish narrows practical availability, so tag it for the provider search.
